Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're getting internal momentum and need to lock a few decisions quickly so procurement can prepare the SOW. Two quick asks before the kickoff:

1) Region: our user base is 70% US (west + central), 25% EU, 5% APAC. Which region should we target as primary for a Dedicated GPU pool to balance latency and cost?

2) Burst/autoscale: our traffic has sharp spikes around product updates — typically a 6x delta for ~15 minutes, once or twice per day. We want a clear recommendation on how to size burst vs reserved capacity and what warm-up / pre-warm expectations are.

3) Billing: procurement wants an example cost profile for a 3-month ramp (commit + burst) and any minimum commit you recommend.

I've attached a simple weekly token profile and a short note on peak windows (delta_weekly_token_profile.csv).

Can we run a short technical/ops handoff this week? Prefer Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

—Sara

Sara — thanks for the data and the clear asks. Looping in CS (Monica), Solutions (Priyom) and Capacity (Kimberly / Rishi) so we can give a consolidated recommendation and set up a short handoff.

High-level answers to unblock procurement and a proposed next step:

- Region recommendation: Given your 70% US footprint we recommend primary in us-west-2 for latency and cost (GPU availability), with eu-west-1 as the secondary region for EU traffic and automated failover. APAC can be served from us-west with higher latency until volumes justify a third region.

- Burst sizing: Based on a stated 6x short spike profile, we typically size reserved capacity for steady-state + 1.5x expected daily average, then allow burst pool size to cover short 6x peaks. That keeps commit modest while avoiding sustained overage. We will propose an initial reserved vGPU commit and a burst permission (minutes / day).

- Warm-up: for models with 1–2s cold starts we recommend a warm-standby policy: keep a small set of hot workers (5–10% of burst) to minimize cold tails for short spikes.

- Billing / ramp: we'll draft a 3-month ramp illustration and include a sample reserved tier + burst unit pricing for procurement.

Next step: propose a 45-minute technical/ops handoff where Priyom and Kimberly walk through model shape, KV/prefix cache expectations, and a skeleton autoscale policy. Can you do Tue 20 Jun 1:00–2:00 PM PT?

Attaching a short proposed agenda for the handoff (proposed_sprint_agenda.pdf).

Thanks,

Diego / team — quick technical clarifications to make the workshop efficient. Sara, replying inline to save time.

On Mon, 18 Jun 2028 at 09:02 Sara Patel <sara@deltahealth.ai> wrote:
> 2) Burst/autoscale: our traffic has sharp spikes around product updates — typically a 6x delta for ~15 minutes, once or twice per day.

Thanks — that profile is clear. A few things we need to know before the handoff:
- Model family and weights: which models will be served (open LLM baseline, custom fine-tune, mixed)? This impacts GPU memory and shard topology.
- Typical sequence length distribution and batchability (are requests independent small prompts or long context chats?)
- Whether you plan to use streaming and function-calling heavily (affects per-token compute).

Suggested autoscale policy (example snippet):
- target_concurrency_per_device: 16–24 (depends on GPU type)
- scale_up_threshold: 0.85 (scale up when avg device utilization > 85% for 60s)
- scale_down_grace: 300s (avoid flapping on 15m spikes)
- burst_bucket_minutes_per_day: 30
- warm_pool_percent: 8

The 15-minute spike that repeats a couple times/day fits a burst_bucket model we use: pre-authorize short minutes of burst at higher per-minute rates while committing less reserved capacity. We'll confirm exact numbers after you share model and seq-lengths.

I can draft a config we can import into Redwood's Dedicated console live during the call.

—Priyom

Quick ops-level plan and recommendation for the upcoming handoff.

Summary recommendations (ops):
- Primary region: us-west-2 (GPU inventory reliability + lower egress to your West US customers).
- Secondary region: eu-west-1 with automated routing rules for EU-subnet traffic and failover TTL of 60s.
- Reserved commit suggestion (initial): 8 A100-equivalent vGPUs (baseline steady + buffer).
- Burst pool: additional 40 A100-equivalent vGPUs available for up to 30 minutes/day initially (covers ~6x short spike if steady usage fits the attached profile).
- Warm-standby: maintain 5% of burst as hot workers; autoscale up in 60–120s (fast path) but keep scale-down grace of 300s to avoid churn.

Operational tradeoffs:
- Lower commit reduces baseline cost but increases per-minute burst unit spend and risk of throttling on sustained spikes >30 minutes.
- Multi-region adds S3 replication & SAC (security) considerations; we'll coordinate with your security team for cross-region key handling.

I've attached a fallback matrix and sample ops runbook we'll use for the handoff (ops_fallback_matrix.xlsx).

Action items we should cover on the call:
- Confirm model shard strategy (Priyom)
- Finalize reserve vs burst numbers and billing cadence for procurement (Diego + Kimberly)
- Security checklist: KMS / audit log retention (Monica + Delta Security)

—Kimberly
